name: Kintampo cowpea evidence
description: Charred cowpeas found in central Ghanaian Kintampo rock shelters are interpreted as evidence of early domesticated cowpea.

date.label: 1830–1595 calibrated BCE (95.5% interval, one cowpea specimen)
date.basis: AMS date on a cowpea cotyledon from B6B horizon 4; the interval is not a date for every specimen or the origin of cultivation.

events.statement: Charred cowpeas found in central Ghanaian Kintampo rock shelters are interpreted as evidence of early domesticated cowpea.

evidence.supports: Charred cowpeas from Kintampo rock shelters in central Ghana date to the second millennium BCE. The authors interpret them as early domesticated cowpea. Only the accessible extract was read; the specific dating and trait methodology requires full-text review.

evidence.locator: pp. 688–689, table 2 and B-sites cowpea remains
evidence.supports: D’Andrea et al. (2007), pp. 688–689, table 2: one cowpea cotyledon from B6B horizon 4 was dated by AMS to 1830–1595 calibrated BCE at 95.5% confidence. The authors identify 16 fragmentary specimens as domesticated cowpea; only three were complete enough for limited measurement, and morphology is compared with domesticated and wild forms. This is evidence from one site, not a demonstrated origin. Selected passages inspected.

events.caveats: One cowpea cotyledon was dated directly; 16 fragmentary specimens were identified by the authors as domesticated, with only three complete enough for limited measurement. The interpretation is not a demonstrated origin.

earliest_record.rationale: Date of this specific documented case, not a claim of global priority.
